clue.text: To Marilyn, A Miller not half struggling in marriage

indicators.note: struggling letters are in disarray, so the pooled letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not half of the name keeps only its first three letters, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: A note addressed to Marilyn Monroe about her husband Arthur Miller and their troubled marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Marilyn Monroe was married to the playwright Arthur Miller, which is the picture. MIL, half of Miller, joins TO MARILYN and A, and 'struggling' rearranges all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes things done within wedlock, so the phrase meaning within the married state fits.

clue.text: Movement of stars described in tabloids got royals in trouble

definitions.text: Movement of stars described in tabloids

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so these nine letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip about royals getting into scrapes, set beside the horoscope page.
explanation.walkthrough: The horoscope column of a tabloid is often headed 'Your stars', so the long definition fits a newspaper picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Horoscope writing claims to read human fortunes from planetary and stellar positions, a staple of popular papers.

clue.text: Large jumper over skirt for modesty

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a jumper here is a kangaroo, a roo for short

indicators.note: the skirt of the word modesty is its edge, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advice to wear a big sweater over a skirt to stay modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater, as the British call it, but it is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spacious has plenty of room, so large in size is a synonym.

clue.text: Male came, no Viagra initially taken

indicators.note: no tells us a letter is removed from the word for came

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Viagra

explanation.surface: A saucy tale of a man who managed without the little blue pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' is the definition, in its sense of no longer single; the surface's innuendo hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is spoken for, or not single, is said to be taken; the idiom means wed.

clue.text: Horrible ladies man primarily ignored beautiful women

indicators.note: horrible means the remaining letters are mangled into a new order
the first letter of each of the two words is ignored, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A dreadful womaniser snubbed by attractive women.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the initials of 'ladies man' leaves ADIES and AN; 'Horrible' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs of Greek myth, lovely female spirits of springs and rivers; this is the classical plural.

clue.text: American coins term for gun going inside range

indicators.note: going inside means one piece is put within another

parts.note: pennies are small coins

indicators.note: term here is a terminus, the end letter of the word gun

explanation.surface: An American paying money for a phrase meaning firearm, which goes into a range, as in a shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests a shooting range to go with the gun; it is the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mountain chain running down the length of Italy, a range of peaks.

clue.text: Escorts picked up in city

indicators.note: picked up is heard, as by a microphone, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to escort someone is to lead them, so escorts means leads

explanation.surface: Companions collected somewhere in town.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England, an example of a city.

clue.text: Boxing result when cut second — one twice knocked out

parts.note: cut means split, as in a cut or split lip

indicators.note: knocked out of shape, the letters of second and the two numerals are rearranged
twice means the numeral is written two times

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fighter cut, his second's efforts failing, and one man knocked out twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing a second is the corner assistant. 'knocked out' rearranges SECOND plus II into DECISION.
explanation.definitionFit: When judges disagree on which boxer won, the verdict delivered is a divided one, an outcome on points.

clue.text: It will probably take poker money fair and square

definitions.text: It will probably take poker money

parts.note: fair dealing is straight, honest
square in the sense of level, flush with a surface

explanation.surface: A poker hand that wins the cash honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair and square' reads as one idiom, but it is two pieces: fair and square each have a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Five consecutive cards of one suit is a near-unbeatable poker hand, so it will usually scoop the pot.

clue.text: Medley in pool — team caught with sprint in the middle

parts.note: a pool of money is the pot, the kitty

indicators.note: caught as in heard, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: team said aloud is teem, which means to pour, as rain does

indicators.note: in the middle picks the two central letters of the word sprint

explanation.surface: A swimming medley relay in the pool with a team sprinting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medley' and 'pool' suggest a swimming race; 'caught' means heard, so team gives teem, meaning POUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed assortment, whether of dried petals or of musical pieces, is a medley.

clue.text: England's opener concerned with boundaries on cricket pitch

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: the boundaries of the word cricket are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An England opening batsman hitting fours on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a cricket ground; it means to set up, as you pitch a tent. In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the field's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a tent is to put it up or raise it, a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Soldiers hiding in plant of dark green colour

indicators.note: hiding in puts the soldiers within the plant

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant with dark green leaves
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops camouflaged among dark green foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark green colour' looks like the definition, but 'of dark green' describes the plant; the colour is off-white.
explanation.definitionFit: This creamy white shade is named after elephant tusk material, a colour name.

clue.text: Individuals entering country for another

indicators.note: entering puts the individuals inside the country

parts.note: the country here is India
individuals are ones, single units

explanation.surface: People crossing one nation's border to reach a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition, meaning another country, beyond the one in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This Southeast Asian archipelago nation is a second country besides India, so 'another' fits the clue's context.

clue.text: Did have to follow doctor that's inundated

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the doctor

parts.note: did have means possessed, owned

explanation.surface: A patient compelled to obey their doctor's advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Being swamped or submerged by water, flooded over, is a synonym.

clue.text: Thoughtless man supporting Nigel for Reform

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means this piece sits beneath the other
reform means to make anew, so the letters are re-formed into another order

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A careless man backing Nigel Farage for his party, Reform UK.
explanation.walkthrough: Reform UK is a British political party led by Nigel Farage, which 'Reform' hints at; here it reshuffles NIGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless or remiss conduct, lacking proper attention, is a synonym for being heedless.

clue.text: Son with appropriate way to provide barrier

parts.note: with means and, in addition
to appropriate is to bag, to take for oneself

explanation.surface: A son with a suitable route to put up a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack filled with sand is a common means of building a defence against floods or gunfire.

clue.text: Flatter borders start to constrict plant

indicators.note: borders means the flattery phrase surrounds the letter

parts.note: to flatter someone is to butter them up

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word constrict

explanation.surface: Flattery hems in a plant's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter borders' reads as more level flower beds; 'Flatter' is a verb meaning BUTTER UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered meadow wildflower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Pass your piece of chicken back — getting space in freezer

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: pass means go, as time passes or goes

indicators.note: piece of points to the first letter of the word chicken

parts.note: an en is a printing space

explanation.surface: A request at dinner to hand over a bit of chicken, with room to spare in the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO + YR + C into CRYOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used to produce very low temperatures is a refrigerant, something that freezes.

clue.text: Tending to go over grass

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: go means run
to grass is to inform, to sing to the police

explanation.surface: Inclined to walk across a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tending to' looks like a phrase meaning inclined to; 'Tending' alone is the definition. GRASS is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for the sick or looking after someone is a synonym of tending.

clue.text: President — idiot making American flyer

parts.note: Bush is a US president, either of the two who held office
tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A jibe at a president as a fool making the Americans look bad.
explanation.definitionFit: This small grey songbird of western North America is a native American bird.

clue.text: Benefits paid for by cutting public transport

indicators.note: cutting means the piece slices into the transport word

parts.note: buses are public transport
if a bill is on you, it is paid for by you

explanation.surface: Welfare money funded by slashing bus services.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra payments or perks are advantages, a synonym for benefits.

clue.text: Keep going south: what rag and bone man wants around east

indicators.note: around means the scrap metal surrounds the letter

parts.words: what rag and bone man wants
parts.note: the rag-and-bone man's street cry was 'any old iron'

explanation.surface: Directions south and east for a scrap collector on his round.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag-and-bone man is a British street trader who collects unwanted household goods and scrap metal from a horse and cart.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere doggedly despite difficulty is an idiom for carrying on.

clue.text: Free rent on leave

parts.note: to let a flat is to rent it out
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Rent-free accommodation while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To release or set loose is a phrasal synonym for freeing.

clue.text: Live sound close to record at first

indicators.note: at first means that letter comes at the start
close to points to the final letter of the word record

parts.note: sound means well, as in sound health

explanation.surface: A live recording with good audio near the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live sound' suggests a concert recording; 'Live' is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside or inhabit a place is a synonym for living there.

clue.text: Tot and adult play

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A toddler and a grown-up playing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a child; it is a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage piece for the theatre is a play, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Odd route when travelling

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so these five are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange path taken on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre or unconventional, beyond the usual bounds, is a borrowed French synonym for strange.

clue.text: Examples of batting positions

parts.note: a side batting in cricket is in
stances are positions or postures

explanation.surface: Illustrations of how a cricketer stands at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cases or occurrences cited to illustrate something are synonyms for examples.

clue.text: Past teams go out: penalties on both sides which are often stuck in the top corner

definitions.text: which are often stuck in the top corner

indicators.note: on here means placed on either side, enclosing the rearranged letters
both sides of the word penalties are its first and last letters
out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Football commentary: former teams go out after penalties placed into the top corner of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: what goes in the top corner is the stamp on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail adhesive labels are customarily placed at the upper right of an envelope.
